newsitem.title: USA: US stocks roar higher after Fed holds rates steady.
newsitem.headline: US stocks roar higher after Fed holds rates steady.

text.p: Wall Street stocks stormed higher on Wednesday, surging in the session's final hour following the Federal Reserve's decision to leave interest rates steady.

The Dow industrials jumped 73 points to close unofficially at 7795, roughly a point short of the blue chip average's all-time closing high of 7796.51. The broad rally carried the Standard & Poor's 500, New York Stock Exchange Composite and Nasdaq Composite indices all to record highs.
The fierce rally caught many analysts by surprise, coming as it did after a Federal Reserve decision that was nearly universally anticipated on Wall Street.
Initially, investors appeared to shrug off the news, but in the final minutes of the session, a series of buy programs virtually seized control of the market.

"It's like a game of hot potato where no one wants to get caught holding cash," said Hugh Johnson, chief investment officer at First Albany. "Whether it's mutual funds or brokerage firms or whomever, we've all learned it's no fun to get caught holding cash in a rising market."
The rally was also remarkable in light of economic indicators still looming -- the closely watched monthly payrolls and wage data, scheduled for release early Thursday.
Because that report is considered one of the most important leading inflation indicators, market reactions have been swift and severe whenever the figures have revealed unexpected strength.
Last July's report was such a case, serving as the trigger point for the stock market's sharp summer-long decline.
However, there was some speculation on Wall Street that the Fed's decision today foreshadowed a tame report on Thursday.

"There's no doubt in my mind the Fed has already had a look at those numbers," said Robert Froehlich, chief investment strategist at Kemper Funds. "It probably means those numbers are going to be tame."

Economists surveyed by Reuters expect the report will show June payrolls rose by 222,000 jobs, up from 138,000 in May. The nation's unemployment rate is expected to hold steady at 4.8 pecent and wages are forecast to rise by 0.4 percent compared with 0.3 percent a month ago.

Once the report is released, traders will have little time to register their response. Markets will hold an abbreviated session ahead of the Independence Day holiday, with the NYSE, AMEX and Nasdaq all slated to close at 1300 EDT/1700 GMT.
Among Dow components, Walt Disney Co fell 1-11/16 to 76-7/8 after Deutsche Morgan Grenfell downgraded the shares to hold, citing concern over ratings at Disney's ABC network.

In other individual issues Pennzoil Co fell 15/16 to 74-7/16 after the integrated oil company rejected a hostile $84 per share takeover bid from Union Pacific Resources Group Inc. Union Pacific Resources fell 1/16 to 24-15/16.
Peritus Software Services Inc PTUS.O was the top percentage gainer on Nasdaq, surging 10-3/4 or 67 percent to 26-3/4 in the first trading after its initial public offering.
Peritus develops software for large-scale computer systems changes like those associated with the year 2000 changeover and the expected conversion to a unified European currency.
Nike Inc fell 5/8 to 57-3/8 after the footwear maker reported second quarter earnings slightly below analysts' estimates.
Several other companies fell sharply after warning about upcoming earnings disappointments.
Friedman's Inc tumbled 6-11/16 to 16-1/16, and IKOS Systems Inc slid 5-1/4 to 15-1/8 after both companies announced fiscal third-quarter results would fall short of expectations.

Networking shares were strong, leading a rally in tech stocks, with Ascend Communications Inc rising 5-5/16 to 49-1/16 and 3Com Corp up 3-11/16 to 48-1/8. Both companies were upgraded by Wall Street firms on Thursday.
The S&P 500 rose 13 points to 904.03, the NYSE Composite gained 5.70 points to 471.71 and the Nasdaq Composite rose 17.36 points to 1455.61, all records.
((-- Wall Street desk, 212-859-1730))
